correctness.rationale: The trace-exponential Hessian is an integral of positive squared norms in every nonzero symmetric direction. Injectivity of the Laplacian parametrization, compactness and orbit symmetry give the unique unrestricted optimizer with common cross and clique conductances. The quotient and two contrast spaces give the four stated eigenvalues. On the budget line the heat trace is strictly convex; its derivative is positive at the all-clique endpoint for r>1, and at the all-cross endpoint has the sign of r−R. This proves the strict support test, including equality. The denominator of R is strictly convex, with initial derivative a₀pq(q−p−2); it decreases throughout when q≤p and increases immediately for q≥p+2. For q=p+1 the unique minimum follows from exp((p+1)a₀t)=(2p+1)/p. Substitution gives the stated peak and expansion. The five-vertex witness's two times were independently bracketed from the orbit marginal costs (0.5622300102912 and 3.1987079650432).
residual_risks: Minor notation mismatch: the Finding introduces u_p and writes ν_p in the peak formula. The proof explicitly defines ν_p=exp(a₀τ_p), which equals u_p, so the exact formula has an unambiguous mathematical reading.
The claim excludes r≤1, t=0, and nonuniform prices within an orbit.

value.rationale: The theorem decides support for all finite times, graph sizes, and premium prices in a natural two-orbit design problem without constraining conductances in advance. It identifies exactly when intermediate-time designs pay for edges omitted by optimal asymptotic-gap designs. The peak law quantifies how narrowly this distinction persists as the family grows.
residual_risks: The mathematical design distinction is not a robustness or empirical performance guarantee.
